$comment: Single source of truth for the wire's transport extent. Machine-readable; TRANSPORTS.md is the prose mirror; the http-mcp MCP `transports` tool returns this verbatim. Rule: raw bytes = wire; framing/routing/negotiation = adapter.
principle: The wire is two atoms: http_request (CALL) and bidi_command (CHANNEL). Every transport reduces to one of these two modes. If a transport carries raw bytes with no application framing, it is wire. If it adds protocol semantics (framing, routing, negotiation), it is an adapter.

modes.CALL: one request, one response, then nothing. Atom: http_request (internal/httpx, net/http).
modes.CHANNEL: one long-lived bidirectional stream. Atom: bidi_command (internal/wsx, hand-rolled RFC6455). SSE/MJPEG are afferent-only (degenerate) channels that ride httpx.

transports.name: http
transports.note: net/http. cmd/wire is a transparent witness proxy; cmd/mcp http_request.

transports.name: websocket
transports.note: internal/wsx hand-rolls the upgrade; cmd/channel holds the BiDi/CDP socket -> broker.

transports.name: sse
transports.note: 8 /feed: text/event-stream + http.Flusher; consumed by EventSource. Server-push, no client->server.

transports.name: unix_socket
transports.note: Same CALL/CHANNEL bytes over a unix dialer instead of tcp. net.Dial("unix",...). No framing -> wire, not adapter. URL: http+unix:///path.sock:/req or ws+unix:///path.sock:/req.

transports.name: grpc
transports.note: unary=CALL, server-stream=CHANNEL over HTTP/2. The .proto + length-prefixed framing are capability-shaped -> adapter.

transports.name: mqtt
transports.note: Persistent broker channel. Topic hierarchy + QoS + retain are application routing -> adapter.

transports.name: webrtc
transports.note: SDP/ICE/DTLS negotiation is capability-shaped (signaled over an httpx CALL); the resulting DataChannel/media is a wsx-style CHANNEL. The wire never sees SDP.

agent_reading_order: 1. Call the http-mcp `transports` tool (or read this transports.json) -> the full 7->2 map in one shot.
2. Need a non-wire transport? Read adapters/<name>/capabilities.json for the dialect deep-dive.
3. Human or fallback? Read TRANSPORTS.md (prose + Mermaid), linked from every repo README.
